headline: AI hit three walls this week: voters, budgets and trust
summary: The limits on AI moved outside the code this week. Voters turned on data centers: 33 of 45 local ballot measures will restrict building, and Texas, the fastest-growing market, may slow its buildout. Budgets tightened too, as Apple cut engineers' daily AI limits from $300 to $200 and Goldman Sachs pulled coding tools from most bankers. The agent toolbox became an attack surface, with poisoned MCP tools fooling agents in 23% of tests and 73 fake agent repos spreading malware. Monday's checking problem still holds, and OpenAI is buying Pierre to build code review for agent-written work. Before you scale agents, know where your compute comes from, what each seat may spend, and who vets every tool they load.

threads.title: Ballot box meets the grid
threads.line: Voters and Texas's governor-elect are turning against data centers. Your compute supply now depends on local politics.

threads.title: Every seat gets a meter
threads.line: Apple and Goldman are rationing AI tools as usage soars. Expect per-person budgets, and decide what an agent is worth.

threads.title: The toolbox is the attack
threads.line: Poisoned tools, fake repos and silent plugin installs show agents inherit every risk in what they load.

threads.title: Found faster than fixed
threads.line: AI made an old PHP crash exploitable and generated patches for 948 kernel flaws in one run. Patch speed is now strategy.

threads.title: Labs buy the review layer
threads.line: OpenAI rebuilt Git for agents and is buying Pierre; Meta took Conductor. Checking agent work is where labs now compete.
